skill.name: set-up-shopware-chatgpt-ads-poas-bidding
skill.description: Configure profit or revenue bidding for a Shopware 6 sales channel in ChatGPT Ads with Product Metrics. Check costs and conversion delivery before switching a campaign.
skill.summary: Use Product Metrics to verify Shopware conversion values and plan profit-based bidding in ChatGPT Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags mark ordinary setup documentation, not system reconnaissance or shell execution. The workflow does use remote tools, reads order data, and lists an unpinned installer. It also permits unsafe key handling and lacks clear safeguards for broader event sharing, consent checks, and profit-based targets.

remediation.issue: Conversions API key may enter chat or tool traces.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exception. Have the operator enter the key only in the verified Product Metrics interface and return only the connection status to the assistant.

remediation.issue: Tracking can be enabled without a specific approval for the destination and event scope.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval of the property, sales channel, Pixel ID, event categories, and customer fields before enabling delivery. Keep the initial delivery check limited to a test order.

remediation.issue: The profit and destination guides do not clearly combine their consent requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Document the required consent for each event and field. Test accepted and denied consent states independently before sending live customer events.

remediation.issue: Order lookup can expose more records and fields than a delivery check requires.
remediation.suggestion: Start with delivery status or an exact test order ID. Restrict returned fields to event status and margin when those fields are needed.

remediation.issue: The documented installation command leaves the runner and skill revision unpinned.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a reviewed runner version and immutable skill revision. Document how to verify the source before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill selects a remote MCP interface without describing a trust check.
remediation.suggestion: Use only an operator-configured, verified connector with the minimum tenant permissions. Do not register a connector based solely on a link in the skill.

remediation.issue: Reported profit values can omit losses and later adjustments.
remediation.suggestion: Label 100 percent as a theoretical threshold. Reconcile conversion values and ad spend against actual contribution margin before recommending a campaign target.

semantic_findings.title: Credential handling conflicts with the browser guide
semantic_findings.description: The skill makes an exception for the OpenAI Conversions API key and tells the agent to pass it to a command. The ads guide says never to paste it into chat. Agent handling can expose the key in prompts or tool arguments even if the assistant never repeats it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception and command handoff are explicit. Their exposure depends on the host, and no actual disclosure was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking activation can share more than the profit event
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs the agent to set up missing tracking and reserves campaign selection for the operator. The destination guide enables sending by default and documents other events, transaction IDs, hashed identifiers, and IP addresses. The workflow provides no explicit approval step for that broader data sharing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented destination sends more than the selected bidding event. The gap concerns approval of event scope, not proof that merchant or shopper authorization was bypassed.

semantic_findings.title: Profit event consent requirements are unclear
semantic_findings.description: The destination guide says nothing is sent without marketing consent. The profit guide describes an opt-out flag when ad personalization consent is absent. It does not clearly state which other consent gates must still pass, risking incorrect setup or verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The descriptions use different consent categories without explaining their combined effect. The documentation shows ambiguity, not an observed consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Reported profit can overstate campaign break-even
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents 100 percent as break-even on profit values. The same guidance sets negative order profit to zero and excludes orders with unknown costs from the profit event. Later refunds do not update events, so reported profit can exceed actual contribution margin.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Zeroing losses and omitting later adjustments can inflate the signal even if event delivery works as documented. The operator still controls the campaign change.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding for Shopware in ChatGPT Ads
content.value_statement: A campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money after product costs, fees, and shipping. Use Product Metrics to verify profit events and decide whether to test profit bidding in one campaign.
actual_capabilities: Check the Product Metrics setup stage through its CLI or MCP connector.
Guide Shopware sales channel pairing and ChatGPT Ads pixel setup.
Explain which Shopware purchase prices and additional costs contribute to the profit event.
Guide a paid test order and distinguish destination validation from successful profit event delivery.
Compare the profit event with the standard revenue event and outline how to select either in Ads Manager.
limitations: Requires a compatible Shopware 6.7 store, Product Metrics Pro, and access to the relevant ad account.
One plugin installation covers one sales channel. The merchant completes Shopware admin steps and chooses the conversion in Ads Manager.
An order with unknown costs has no profit event. Losses are reported as zero, and later refunds do not revise sent events.
This workflow does not set up bidding on new customers, returning customers, or lifetime value.

use_cases.title: Prepare a store for profit tracking
use_cases.description: Check platform requirements, choose a sales channel, and confirm which costs Product Metrics needs before measuring order profit.

use_cases.title: Pilot profit bidding on one campaign
use_cases.description: Compare the revenue and profit events, then plan a manual campaign change after confirming the test event in Ads Manager.

use_cases.title: Validate reported profit before setting a target
use_cases.description: Compare contribution margin from store records with the value reported for ads. Identify gaps from missing costs, losses, and later refunds.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the difference
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain profit and revenue bidding for my Shopware store. List what I need before setup. Do not connect any accounts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the two bidding signals.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for [Property] and [Sales Channel] with read-only access. List what is complete and what I must do in each app.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: resume setup without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a missing profit event
prompt_templates.prompt: My paid test order sent revenue but no profit event. Use delivery status and my test order ID [ID] only. List cost and consent checks without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: diagnose event delivery in a paired channel.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a one-campaign pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my current POAS of [Value] to suggest a provisional target for [Campaign]. Explain how zero-value losses and later refunds may affect it. Leave campaign settings unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan the switch after verifying profit tracking.

output_examples.input: The destination accepted a test event. Is profit bidding ready?
output: The destination check passed, but it does not show up in Ads Manager reporting.
Verify that a paid test order with the required consent and complete costs produced the profit event.
Select the profit conversion manually only after it appears in Ads Manager.

output_examples.input: My paid test order shows revenue but no profit. What should I check?
output: Check the purchase price on each Shopware order line and confirm that additional costs are active.
Check for missing cost inputs and confirm that the test order meets the required consent conditions.
Place a new test order after correcting the setup. Keep the campaign on its current conversion until the profit event arrives.

output_examples.input: My campaign measures 1.5 in profit value per unit of ad spend. What target should I consider?
output: Consider 150 percent as a provisional target, not a guarantee.
Compare the profit value with actual contribution margin first because reported values can exclude losses and later refunds.
Test one campaign and review the results after a few weeks.

best_practices: Confirm the intended sales channel, property, ad pixel, and event data before enabling delivery.
Enter API keys and pairing tokens only in verified setup interfaces, never in chat or terminal arguments.
Verify a paid test order, confirm the consent settings, and review actual contribution margin before switching a campaign.
anti_patterns: Treating destination validation as proof that a profit event arrived in Ads Manager.
Reusing a revenue-based target after switching to profit without checking the actual margin.
Listing live customer orders when delivery status or one test order is enough.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Product Metrics Pro and its Shopware plugin. You also need access to the Product Metrics property and ChatGPT Ads Manager.

faq.question: Which Shopware versions does this workflow cover?
faq.answer: The guide documents Shopware 6.7 with PHP 8.2 or later and lists plugin build compatibility with Shopware 6.7.14.0. Shopware 5 is not supported.

faq.question: Which event should I use for profit or revenue?
faq.answer: For profit, create a conversion using pm_order_profit and select it manually in Ads Manager. For revenue, use the standard order_created event.

faq.question: Why does a paid order have revenue but no profit event?
faq.answer: Profit requires complete costs. Check the purchase prices, additional costs, and consent settings. An order with a known loss sends a zero profit value.

faq.question: Does this resend older orders or update later refunds?
faq.answer: No. Historical orders are not imported, events older than seven days are not accepted, and later refunds do not update sent conversions.

faq.question: Does the assistant choose the conversion for me?
faq.answer: No. The assistant can explain and verify the setup, but you choose the campaign conversion and target in ChatGPT Ads Manager.
